program.description: SRAP is a state funded programme that provides housing subsidies on behalf of very low-income New Jersey residents. Applicants must be New Jersey residents, must be at least 18 years old or an emancipated minor, and must meet the income limit of the county where they will live - the limits are published per county for households of up to eight people. Placement on the waiting list is by lottery, with preferences for veterans and their surviving spouses, people who are homeless, elderly or disabled, and local residents. At the time of writing the pre-application period is closed.
program.plain_language_summary: SRAP is a New Jersey rent subsidy for people with very low incomes. You have to live in New Jersey, be 18 or older, and earn under the limit for your county and household size. Places are given out by lottery from a waiting list, and the waiting list is closed right now - check the official page for the next opening.
who_it_helps: New Jersey renters with very low income
Veterans and their surviving spouses, who get the highest priority
People who are homeless, elderly or disabled

sources.title: State Rental Assistance Program (SRAP)
sources.publisher: New Jersey Department of Community Affairs, Division of Housing and Community Resources
sources.excerpt:
The New Jersey State Rental Assistance Program (SRAP) is a state funded program that provides housing subsidies on behalf of very low-income New Jersey residents, for decent, safe and sanitary housing. Persons applying must meet all applicable SRAP income and eligibility requirements. A total of 6,000 households will be selected through a lottery system to be placed on the State Rental Assistance Program waiting list. You must be eighteen (18) years of age or older or be an emancipated minor to apply. Please note that only New Jersey residents are eligible to apply for SRAP assistance.

At the time of selection from the State Rental Assistance Program waiting list, applicants must meet the income limits of the county where they will be residing and provide proof of New Jersey residency. The Income Limits below represent the guidelines up to 8 household members. If you have a larger household, please contact DCA at 609-292-4080, select Option 9 for assistance in determining the maximum income limits for your household. The below Income Limits Chart show the income limits that are in effect now.
2024 STATE RENTAL ASSISTANCE PROGRAM INCOME LIMITS

The SRAP waiting list opening for pre-applications has closed.
Please continue to check DCA’s website to see when new waiting lists will be opened in the future.

program.description: The Section 8 Housing Choice Voucher programme makes private market rental housing affordable by paying a rent subsidy directly to the landlord. It is funded by the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development and is built on the premise that housing costs - rent and utilities - should not exceed 30 percent of a household's income. Assistance goes to low and very low-income households. The statewide programme run by DCA is available to residents of all New Jersey counties, and municipal and county housing authorities administer their own Section 8 Existing Housing programmes. Income limits are published per county for households of one to eight people.
program.plain_language_summary: A Section 8 voucher pays part of your rent straight to your landlord, so your rent and utilities come to about 30 percent of your income. Income limits depend on your county and household size. You can apply through the state programme or through your county or town housing authority when their waiting list opens.
who_it_helps: Renters with low or very low income
Households paying more than they can afford in rent
Residents of any New Jersey county

sources.publisher: New Jersey Department of Community Affairs, Division of Housing and Community Resources
sources.excerpt:
The Section 8 Housing Voucher Program assists in making safe and quality housing in the private rental market affordable to low, and very low-income households by reducing housing costs through direct rent subsidy payments to landlords. The program is funded by the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development.
Section 8 HCV program is based on the premise that housing costs (rent and utilities) should not exceed 30 percent of a household's income.
Assistance is provided to low, and very low-income households and individuals.
The statewide program is available to residents of all New Jersey counties. Section 8 Existing Housing programs are administered throughout the State by a number of municipal and county authorities. Click the link below to see the list of county authorities directory.
